mainTopic: Crushed testicles, removing blood from meat, the two nerves of the גיד הנשה, butchers and leftover חלב, and sending a thigh to a non-Jew.
overview: The amud opens in the middle of an argument about crushed testicles. One side says they never heal, so they count as אבר מן החי. The other side says they never rot, so they are still alive. רבי יוחנן rules that they are permitted, but tells רב שמן בר אבא to keep his home's strict custom. Next come rules about removing blood: young goats' testicles, then raw meat, testicles and neck veins placed on coals, where the הלכה follows the lenient view of רב אחא. After that, an animal's head is placed in hot ashes, and what matters is whether the blood has a way out. The גמרא then returns to the גיד הנשה. שמואל says it has two nerves, and the גמרא settles two ברייתות against him. Next it rules how much leftover חלב gets a butcher lashes (a כזית) or removed from his job (a barley grain). It also explains, in two versions, why butchers' trustworthiness changed over the generations. Finally a new משנה allows sending a whole thigh with the גיד הנשה to a non-Jew. The גמרא begins to ask what case the משנה means, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why one opinion forbids crushed testicles
steps.stepSummary: The forbidding opinion reasons that because crushed testicles never heal, they count as an אבר מן החי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they do not heal, they are considered a limb from a living animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reasoning of the opinion that forbids eating an animal's crushed testicles. Since they never heal, they are treated as a limb that is already 'cut off' while the animal is alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The testicles are still physically attached, but because they can never recover, this opinion views them as dead and separated. Something separated from a living animal is אבר מן החי, so שחיטה does not permit it. The opening words of the sentence, saying whose opinion this is, came just before this section begins.

keyTerms.meaning: a limb taken from a living animal, which is forbidden even after the animal is slaughtered
crushed testicles (the subject of this whole argument)

steps.confusionAlert: The word בֵּיעֵי usually means 'eggs,' but here it means testicles. The whole section is about an animal's testicles, not eggs.

phrases.english: since they do not heal,
these are a limb from a living animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of the dispute about crushed testicles, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Crushed testicles never heal, so the forbidding opinion treats them as אבר מן החי.

steps.title: Why the other opinion permits crushed testicles
steps.stepSummary: The permitting opinion reasons that because crushed testicles do not rot, there is still life in them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who permits says: since they do not rot, there is life in them.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא gives the reasoning of the opinion that permits crushed testicles. Dead flesh would rot, so the fact that they stay fresh shows they are still alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opinion uses a different piece of evidence: no rotting. If there is still life in them, they are a living part of the animal and not אבר מן החי. So שחיטה permits them along with the rest of the animal.

phrases.english: The one who permits: since they do not rot,
these have life in them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite opinion's reasoning, using different evidence.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Crushed testicles do not rot, so the permitting opinion holds that they still have life and are permitted.

steps.title: The forbidding opinion explains why they don't rot
steps.stepSummary: The forbidding opinion answers the 'no rotting' evidence: they stay fresh only because air cannot reach them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other opinion says: the fact that they do not rot is because air does not reach them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the forbidding opinion handles the permitting opinion's evidence. Its answer is that they don't rot simply because they are sealed off from the air, not because they are alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permitting side claimed 'no rotting' proves there is life. The forbidding side says there is another cause: rotting needs air, and the testicles are closed off inside the body. So the evidence proves nothing about life.

phrases.english: And the other: this, that they do not rot —
phrases.notes: 'The other' here is the one who forbids. He is answering the permitter's evidence.

phrases.english: is because air does not reach them,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The forbidding side defends itself against the evidence brought in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives another cause for the opposing side's evidence.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No rotting might seem to prove the testicles are alive.
steps.terutzMaskana: No rotting is only because air cannot reach them, so it does not prove life.

steps.title: The permitting opinion explains why they don't heal
steps.stepSummary: The permitting opinion answers the 'no healing' evidence: they fail to heal only because they are weakened, not because they are dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other opinion says: the fact that they do not heal is because weakness has taken hold of them.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the permitting opinion handles the forbidding opinion's evidence. They don't heal because they have become weak, but they are still alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidding side said 'no healing' proves they are dead and count as אבר מן החי. The permitting side says not healing only shows weakness, not death. So each side has an answer to the other's proof, and the next step gives רבי יוחנן's practical ruling.

phrases.english: And the other: this, that they do not heal —
phrases.notes: Now 'the other' is the one who permits, answering the forbidder's evidence.

phrases.english: it is weakness that has taken hold of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 3. The permitting side now defends itself against the evidence in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives another cause for the opposing side's evidence.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No healing might seem to prove the testicles are dead, an אבר מן החי.
steps.terutzMaskana: No healing only shows weakness. They are still alive.
steps.whatToRemember: Forbidder: 'they never heal, so they're dead (אבר מן החי)'; he explains 'no rotting' as 'no air.' Permitter: 'they never rot, so they're alive'; he explains 'no healing' as 'just weakness.'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: permitted, but not for you
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells רב שמן בר אבא that crushed testicles are permitted, but he personally should not eat them because of 'do not forsake the Torah of your mother.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to רב שמן בר אבא: Crushed testicles are permitted, but you should not eat them, because of the verse 'And do not forsake the Torah of your mother.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן rules that crushed testicles are permitted. He still tells רב שמן בר אבא not to eat them himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic הלכה follows the permitting opinion. However, 'the Torah of your mother' is understood as the custom of the place you come from. רב שמן בר אבא came from a place that was strict about this, so he should keep that strictness.

keyTerms.meaning: 'do not forsake the Torah of your mother,' used here to mean: keep your family's or home's custom

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the difference between what is permitted by law and what a person should do because of a custom he has received.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to Rav Shemen bar Abba:
These crushed testicles are permitted,
but you should not eat them
because of: 'And do not forsake the Torah of your mother.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַב שֶׁמֶן בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical ruling on the dispute in steps 1 through 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Crushed testicles are permitted, but someone from a place with a strict custom should keep it.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי on young goats' testicles
steps.stepSummary: Testicles of a young goat may be eaten without peeling up to thirty days. After that, it depends on whether they contain semen.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: Testicles of young goats, up to thirty days old, are permitted without peeling. From then on, if they contain semen they are forbidden, and if not, they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new rule about testicles. מר בר רב אשי rules on when a young goat's testicles may be eaten without peeling off their covering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until thirty days, they may be eaten as they are, without peeling. After thirty days, the deciding factor is whether they have developed semen. If they have, they are forbidden. If not, they are still permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: from here on, after that point

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
These testicles of young goats,

phrases.aramaic: עַד תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין שַׁרְיָין בְּלָא קְלִיפָה,
phrases.english: up to thirty days they are permitted without peeling,
from this point on —
if they have semen, they are forbidden,
and if they do not have semen, they are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related topic about testicles.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Up to 30 days, a young goat's testicles are permitted without peeling. After that, it depends on whether they contain semen.

steps.title: How do we know if there is semen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how one can tell whether the testicles contain semen.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question about the rule just given. It is setting up the next step, which explains how to check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on whether there is semen, but that cannot be seen directly. So the גמרא asks for a sign someone can actually check.

phrases.english: How do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to apply the rule from step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A visible sign that shows whether the testicles contain semen.

steps.title: Red streaks are the sign
steps.stepSummary: If there are red streaks, they are forbidden. If there are none, they are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they have red streaks, they are forbidden. If they do not have red streaks, they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a simple visual test: look for red streaks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Red streaks are the sign that the testicles have developed semen, so they fall into the forbidden category from step 6. Without red streaks, they are treated as not having semen and are permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: Young goat testicles: permitted without peeling up to 30 days. After that, red streaks mean forbidden, and no red streaks mean permitted.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אִית בְּהוּ שׁוּרְיָיקֵי סוּמָּקֵי – אֲסִירָן,
phrases.english: if they have red streaks in them, they are forbidden;
if they do not have red streaks in them, they are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Red streaks show semen, so they are forbidden. No red streaks means they are permitted.

steps.title: A dispute about raw meat, testicles, and neck veins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רב אחא and רבינא disagree about three items: raw meat, testicles, and the large veins of the neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: About raw meat, testicles, and neck veins, רב אחא and רבינא disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names three items that רב אחא and רבינא argue about. This is a setup line: it does not yet explain what they argue about. That comes a little later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three items hold a lot of blood, so the question is how that blood can be removed. The גמרא first lists the dispute and then pauses to tell us whose view is the הלכה. Only afterward does it explain the details (step 12).

keyTerms.meaning: The large blood veins of the neck

phrases.english: Raw meat, testicles, and neck veins:
Rav Acha and Ravina disagree about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of young goats' testicles to a wider dispute about removing blood from three blood-heavy items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אחא and רבינא dispute the הלכה of raw meat, testicles, and neck veins.

steps.title: The rule for deciding between רב אחא and רבינא
steps.stepSummary: Across the Torah, רבינא is the lenient one and the הלכה follows him. In these three cases it is reversed: רב אחא is lenient and the הלכה follows רב אחא.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the whole Torah, רבינא is lenient and רב אחא is strict, and the הלכה follows רבינא's lenient view. The exception is these three cases: here רב אחא is lenient and רבינא is strict, and the הלכה follows רב אחא's lenient view.
steps.whatsHappening: Before explaining the dispute, the גמרא gives a rule for deciding who is right. In these three cases the lenient view is the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when we are not told who holds which view, we assume רבינא is lenient and follow him. Here the roles are switched, but the outcome stays the same: the lenient view wins. This matters later, because step 12 only says 'one says, one says.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule tells us the practical outcome for all three items: we follow the lenient opinion.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the הלכה follows רבינא here as usual. In these three cases רב אחא is the lenient one, and the הלכה follows him.

phrases.english: In the entire Torah,
phrases.notes: He means all the other disputes between these two sages.

phrases.english: Ravina is lenient and Rav Acha is strict,
and the law follows Ravina, to be lenient,
except for these three,
where Rav Acha is lenient and Ravina is strict,
and the law follows Rav Acha, to be lenient.

steps.triggerLanguage: בכל התורה כולה רבינא לקולא ורב אחא לחומרא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the deciding rule for the dispute named in step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In these three cases, רב אחא is lenient and the הלכה follows him.

steps.title: Salting or roasting on a spit removes the blood
steps.stepSummary: Raw meat that turned red with blood is permitted if it is cut and salted, even for cooking in a pot. Hanging it on a spit to roast also works, because the blood drips out.
steps.simpleTranslation: Raw meat that turned red: if one cut it and salted it, it is fine even for a pot. If one hung it on a spit, that is also fine, because the blood drips out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the cases. It starts with the methods everyone agrees work: salting, and roasting on a spit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Salt pulls blood out, so the meat may even go into a pot afterward. Hanging the meat on a spit lets the blood flow down and out. These agreed cases set the background for the disputed case of coals.

phrases.english: Raw meat that turned red,
if he cut it and salted it,
even for a pot it is also fine.
If he hung it on a spit, it is also fine,
because the blood drips out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the cases behind the dispute in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salting reddened raw meat, or roasting it on a spit, removes the blood and permits it.

steps.title: Meat placed on coals: does the blood come out?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא and רבינא argue about meat placed on coals. One says the coals draw the blood out; the other says the coals shrivel the meat and trap the blood. The same dispute applies to testicles and neck veins.
steps.simpleTranslation: On coals, רב אחא and רבינא disagree. One says the coals draw out the blood. The other says the coals shrink the meat and close it up. The same applies to testicles and to neck veins.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual dispute from step 9: does putting raw meat on coals let the blood out or lock it in?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is what the heat of coals does. One view says it draws the blood out like a spit does. The other says it seals the meat so the blood stays inside. From step 10, we know רב אחא holds the lenient view here, so the הלכה is that coals do draw out the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: They shrivel and close up (the meat)

steps.whatToRemember: In all three cases (raw meat, testicles, neck veins), the dispute is about coals. Using step 10, the הלכה follows the lenient view, which is רב אחא's: the coals draw the blood out.

phrases.english: On coals:
Rav Acha and Ravina disagree about it.
One says: they draw it out,
and one says: they shrink it closed.
phrases.notes: If the meat closes up, the blood is trapped inside, so the meat would be forbidden.

phrases.english: And the same for testicles, and the same for neck veins.

steps.triggerLanguage: אגומרי פליגי בה רב אחא ורבינא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the agreed cases (salt, spit), it presents the disputed case: coals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute whether coals draw out blood or seal it in. By the rule in step 10, the lenient view is the הלכה.

steps.title: An animal's head in hot ashes: which way it lies matters
steps.stepSummary: A head placed in hot ashes with the slaughter cut facing down is permitted, because the blood drips out. If it lies on its side, the blood congeals and it is forbidden. If it lies on its nostrils, it is permitted only if something was put in the nostrils to keep them open.
steps.simpleTranslation: A head in hot ashes: if he placed it on the place of slaughter, the blood drips out and it is permitted. On its sides, the blood congeals and it is forbidden. If he placed it on its nostrils: if he stuck something into them, it is permitted; if not, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: Since we are talking about heat and blood, the גמרא adds a related case: an animal's head put in hot ashes, for example to remove its hair. It depends on whether the blood has a way out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key idea is an opening for the blood. The slaughter cut is an open exit, so the blood drips out. On the sides there is no opening, so the blood congeals inside. The nostrils work only if something holds them open.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where the animal was slaughtered (the neck cut)
It congeals (the blood thickens and stays in)

phrases.english: A head in hot ashes:
if he placed it on the place of slaughter,
the blood drips out and it is permitted.
On the sides, it congeals and it is forbidden.
If he placed it on its nostrils,
if he stuck something into it, it is permitted,
phrases.notes: Something put in the nostrils keeps them open so the blood can flow out.

phrases.english: and if not, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: From meat placed on coals, the גמרא moves to a related case: a head placed in hot ashes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughter cut down: permitted. Sides: forbidden. Nostrils: permitted only if they were kept open.

steps.title: A second version of the head-in-ashes rule
steps.stepSummary: Another version says that a head placed on the nostrils or on the slaughter cut is permitted, because the blood drips out. Only on the sides does it depend on whether something was stuck in to open a path.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: on its nostrils or on the place of slaughter, the blood drips out. On the sides, if he stuck something into it, it is permitted; if not, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second tradition about the head in ashes. This version is more lenient about the nostrils and the sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the nostrils count as a natural opening just like the slaughter cut, so nothing needs to be inserted. Even the sides can be permitted if something is stuck in to open a path. In the first version, the sides were always forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree that blood must have an exit. They differ on whether the nostrils are open enough by themselves, and whether the sides can be fixed by inserting something.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
On its nostrils or on the place of slaughter, it drips out,

phrases.aramaic: אַצְּדָדִין – אִי דָּץ בֵּיהּ מִידֵּי – שְׁרֵי,
phrases.english: on the sides, if he stuck something into it, it is permitted,
and if not, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: איכא דאמרי אנחיריה ואבית השחיטה דאיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, more lenient version of the rules in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nostrils or slaughter cut down: permitted. Sides: permitted only if something was inserted to open a path for the blood.

steps.title: There are two nerves: the inner one carries punishment, the outer one does not
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the גיד הנשה includes two nerves. The inner one, next to the bone, is forbidden and one is punished for eating it. The outer one, next to the flesh, is forbidden but one is not punished.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: There are two nerves. The inner one, next to the bone, is forbidden, and one is liable for eating it. The outer one, next to the flesh, is forbidden, but one is not liable for eating it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the גיד הנשה and brings שמואל's rule that there are two nerves with different levels of איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both nerves must be removed, but they are not equal. Only the inner nerve, by the bone, is the real Torah-level גיד הנשה that brings punishment. The outer nerve is forbidden at a lower level, so there is no punishment for eating it.

keyTerms.meaning: The sciatic nerve, which the Torah forbids us to eat
One is liable (punished) for eating it

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the description of the two nerves that the next two questions will test against ברייתות.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
There are two nerves:
the inner one, next to the bone,
is forbidden, and one is liable for it;
the outer one, next to the flesh,
is forbidden, but one is not liable for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל, שְׁנֵי גִּידִין הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of blood in meat (steps 11–14) and returns to the גיד הנשה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The inner nerve, by the bone, is forbidden with punishment. The outer nerve, by the flesh, is forbidden without punishment.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the inner nerve is next to the flesh
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes the inner nerve as being next to the flesh, which seems to contradict שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: the inner nerve is next to the flesh!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל with a ברייתא that places the inner nerve next to the flesh, not next to the bone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said the inner, Torah-level nerve is by the bone. The ברייתא puts it by the flesh, so the two descriptions seem to clash.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: the inner one is next to the flesh!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's location of the inner nerve.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that the inner nerve is next to the bone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא describes the inner nerve as next to the flesh, which is the opposite of what שמואל said.

steps.title: The inner nerve bores into the flesh
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that the inner nerve starts by the bone but bores into the flesh, so both descriptions are true.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא said in the name of רב כהנא: It bores in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the inner nerve sits by the bone but also reaches into the flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in שמואל's rule changes. The nerve's path explains both sources: it lies against the bone, and it also burrows into the meat, so the ברייתא can call it next to the flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: It surely bores or burrows in

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha said that Rav Kahana said:
It bores in.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the inner nerve, the one lying by the bone. It burrows into the flesh too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: אִיקְּלוֹדֵי מִיקְּלִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the ברייתא's description: both locations are true
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא puts the inner nerve in a completely different place than שמואל does.
steps.terutzMaskana: The inner nerve is by the bone but bores into the flesh, so the ברייתא and שמואל agree.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the outer nerve is next to the bone
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא describes the outer nerve as next to the bone, again seemingly against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: the outer nerve that is next to the bone!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second challenge, this time about the outer nerve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל placed the outer nerve by the flesh. This ברייתא places it by the bone. The answer of boring into the flesh does not help here, so a new answer is needed.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: the outer one, which is next to the bone!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to שמואל, now about the outer nerve.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that the outer nerve is next to the flesh
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the outer nerve is next to the bone, the opposite of שמואל.

steps.title: Where butchers open the leg, the outer nerve is by the bone
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that the ברייתא is speaking about the spot where butchers cut open the leg. At that spot the outer nerve is close to the bone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: The ברייתא means the place where the butchers open up the leg.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is describing one particular spot, where butchers cut in to reveal the nerve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In general the outer nerve is by the flesh, as שמואל said. Only at the place where butchers cut the leg open does it come close to the bone, and that is the spot the ברייתא is describing.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's picture stands: the inner nerve (Torah-level) is by the bone, and the outer nerve (lower level) is by the flesh. Both ברייתות are explained without changing it.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Where the butchers open it up.
phrases.notes: He means the spot where butchers cut the leg open. There the outer nerve lies close to the bone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: הֵיכָא דְּפָרְעִי טַבָּחֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a specific location
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says the outer nerve is by the bone everywhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only at the spot where butchers open the leg is the outer nerve by the bone.

steps.title: How much leftover חלב makes a butcher responsible
steps.stepSummary: A butcher cleaned out the חלב, but some forbidden fat was found after him. רב יהודה says he is responsible if it is the size of a barley grain. רבי יוחנן says only if it is a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: A butcher after whom forbidden fat was found: רב יהודה says the measure is a barley grain; רבי יוחנן says the measure is a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: an argument about how much leftover חלב makes the butcher who cleaned the meat responsible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that a butcher can be held responsible for חלב he missed. They argue about the amount. רב יהודה is stricter, with the tiny size of a barley grain. רבי יוחנן requires a full כזית, the normal eating measure.

keyTerms.meaning: The size of a barley grain
The size of an olive, the standard eating measure

phrases.english: It was stated: a butcher
after whom forbidden fat was found,
Rav Yehuda says: with the size of a barley grain;
Rabbi Yochanan says: with an olive-size.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic after the discussion of the two nerves ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה: a butcher is responsible for leftover חלב the size of a barley grain. רבי יוחנן: only for a כזית.

steps.title: רב פפא: Lashes versus Losing the Job
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that רב יהודה and רבי יוחנן do not argue. A כזית is the amount for מלקות, and a barley grain is the amount for removing the טבח from his job.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: They do not really argue. One opinion is talking about giving the butcher lashes. The other is talking about removing him from his job.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא takes the argument from the last step and shows that both opinions can be true at once. Each one is talking about a different punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's כזית is the amount needed for real Torah-level punishment, which is מלקות. רב יהודה's barley grain is a smaller amount, and it is enough to fire the butcher for being careless. So the two numbers answer two different questions.

keyTerms.meaning: To remove him from his position as butcher

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: And they do not disagree.
Here, it is about giving him lashes;
phrases.notes: This first 'here' is רבי יוחנן's כזית.

phrases.english: there, it is about removing him from his job.
phrases.notes: This second 'there' is רב יהודה's barley grain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Harmonizes the two opinions given in step 20
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה and רבי יוחנן seem to disagree about the amount that makes the butcher responsible.
steps.terutzMaskana: A כזית is the amount for מלקות. A barley grain is the amount for firing him.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: One Spot versus Several Spots
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא gives a different way to show the two opinions do not argue. A barley grain counts when it is all in one place. A כזית counts even when it is spread over two or three places.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: A barley grain's worth makes him responsible if it is all in one spot. An olive's worth makes him responsible even if it is spread out over two or three spots.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא offers a second way to make peace between רב יהודה and רבי יוחנן. In his view they are talking about different situations, not different punishments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the leftover fat sits all together, even a small barley-sized piece shows the butcher was careless. If small bits are scattered around, he is only responsible once they add up to a כזית. So each opinion fits a different case.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
A barley grain's size, when it is in one place;
an olive's size, even when it is in two or three places.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: כִּשְׂעוֹרָה בְּמָקוֹם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different way from רב פפא to harmonize the two opinions
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different cases (fat in one spot versus scattered fat)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The barley grain and the כזית seem to be two competing amounts for the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The barley grain applies to fat all in one spot. The כזית applies to fat scattered in several spots.

steps.title: The Final הלכה on Leftover Fat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that a טבח gets מלקות only for a כזית, but he is removed from his job even for a barley grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: to give him lashes, it must be an olive's size. To remove him from his job, a barley grain's size is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling. It follows רב פפא's approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling uses the same two-punishment split that רב פפא suggested. Real Torah punishment needs the full כזית. Losing his job is a protective step, so a smaller amount is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is (the final practical ruling)

steps.whatToRemember: A butcher who leaves חלב behind gets מלקות only for a כזית, but he is fired even for a barley grain.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical standard for holding a butcher responsible when he removes חלב carelessly.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: to give him lashes, it must be an olive's size;
to remove him from his job, a barley grain's size is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules in line with רב פפא's harmonization
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: מלקות requires a כזית. Removal from the job requires only a barley grain.

steps.title: Butchers Became Believed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that says butchers are not believed about removing the גיד הנשה. רבי יוחנן reports that the ruling later changed, and they are believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Butchers are not believed, etc.' רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They changed their minds and said butchers are believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new line of the משנה, about whether we trust a טבח who says he removed the גיד הנשה. רבי יוחנן reports that the ruling changed over time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the ruling was that butchers could not be trusted on this. Later it was changed to say they can be trusted. This change will set up רב נחמן's question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They changed their minds and said

phrases.english: Butchers are not believed, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה about the גיד הנשה. The word in square brackets means 'and so on' and is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
They changed their minds and said they are believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Butchers were first not believed about the גיד הנשה, but the ruling changed to say they are believed.

steps.title: Did People Get Better?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks whether later generations improved, since otherwise there is no reason butchers should suddenly become trustworthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Did the generations get better?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges רבי יוחנן's report. Why would butchers suddenly become trustworthy?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we assume later generations are not more careful than earlier ones. So a change from 'not believed' to 'believed' seems strange. רב נחמן wants to know what changed.

keyTerms.meaning: Have the generations become more worthy?

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Did the generations improve?
phrases.notes: He means: are butchers today really more honest than before?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the change reported in step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's report that butchers later became believed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unless people became more trustworthy, which is unlikely, there is no reason for the ruling to change.

steps.title: The הלכה Changed, Not the People
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that at first the הלכה followed רבי מאיר, whose method of removing the nerve is hard work, so butchers were not trusted. Later it followed רבי יהודה's easier method, so they could be trusted.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, when they held like רבי מאיר, butchers were not believed. In the end they held like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב נחמן's question. The people did not change. The הלכה about how to remove the nerve changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי מאיר, removing the גיד הנשה needs hard digging, so a butcher might skip it. Under רבי יהודה, the job is much easier. With the easier rule, there was no longer a reason to suspect butchers, so they became believed.
steps.whatToRemember: Butchers became believed about the גיד הנשה because the הלכה moved to רבי יהודה's easier method of removing it, not because people became more honest.
steps.confusionAlert: The change is not about butchers becoming more honest. It is about the job becoming easier once the הלכה followed רבי יהודה.

phrases.aramaic: מֵעִיקָּרָא דַּהֲווֹ סָבְרִי לַהּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר –
phrases.english: At first, when they held like Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier argument about whether you must dig around the flesh to get out the nerve's roots.

phrases.english: they were not believed;
but in the end they held like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִיקָּרָא דַּהֲווֹ סָבְרִי לַהּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's challenge in step 25
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The change seemed to mean that butchers had become more trustworthy.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling changed because the הלכה moved from רבי מאיר's hard method to רבי יהודה's easy method, so there was less reason to suspect butchers.

steps.title: A second version: the ruling changed to 'not believed'
steps.stepSummary: Some teach the discussion on the end of the משנה, where חכמים say butchers are believed about the גיד הנשה and the חלב. רבי יוחנן reports that they later changed this and said butchers are not believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some people teach this discussion on the end of the משנה: 'And the חכמים say: they are believed about it and about the חלב.' רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: they changed their minds and said butchers are not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of what רבי יוחנן said. In this version he is talking about the חכמים in the end of the משנה, and the change goes in the opposite direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (step 24), the ruling went from 'not believed' to 'believed.' Here it starts at 'believed,' which is the view of the חכמים, and changes to 'not believed.' The rest of this version will follow from this reversed starting point.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach it this way; it introduces a second version of the discussion
The end part of a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix the two versions! In the first version, butchers went from NOT believed to believed. In this version, they go from believed to NOT believed, and then רב נחמן brings them back to believed.

phrases.english: There are those who teach it on the end of the משנה:
And the חכמים say:
They are believed about it and about the forbidden fat.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
They changed their minds and said they are not believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רבי יוחנן's report from step 24, attached to the end of the משנה and going in the opposite direction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to this version, the ruling changed from the חכמים's 'believed' to 'not believed.'

steps.title: רב נחמן: nowadays butchers are believed
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says that in our times butchers are believed again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: nowadays they are believed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן adds a third stage: today, butchers are trusted again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So in this version there are three stages: believed, then not believed, then believed again 'nowadays.' This sets up the next question: what changed in our times?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה נֶאֱמָנִין.
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: Nowadays they are believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה נֶאֱמָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a later stage after רבי יוחנן's 'not believed.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רב נחמן's time, butchers are believed about removing the גיד הנשה.

steps.title: Did the later generations get better?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: are later generations more honest, so that butchers can now be believed?
steps.simpleTranslation: Have the generations improved?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן: why should butchers today be trusted when earlier butchers were not?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we assume later generations are not better than earlier ones. So if earlier butchers were not trusted, it seems strange that today's butchers would be, unless something else changed.

phrases.english: Have the generations improved?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's statement from step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that butchers are believed nowadays.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Later generations are not more honest, so there is no reason butchers should suddenly become trustworthy.

steps.title: The switch from רבי יהודה to רבי מאיר, and the butchers forgot
steps.stepSummary: At first the הלכה followed רבי יהודה, then it switched to רבי מאיר. While butchers still remembered רבי יהודה's easy way, they were not trusted. Now that they forgot it, they are trusted.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first they held like רבי יהודה, then they switched to hold like רבי מאיר. As long as the butchers remembered רבי יהודה's view, they were not believed. But now that they have forgotten רבי יהודה's view, they are believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the butchers did not become more honest. What changed is that they forgot the old easier method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the הלכה followed רבי יהודה, butchers were trusted, since his method is easy. When the הלכה switched to רבי מאיר's harder method, butchers who still remembered רבי יהודה might rely on the old easy way, so they were not trusted. Once רבי יהודה's view was forgotten, butchers only knew רבי מאיר's way and did it properly, so they could be trusted again.

keyTerms.meaning: Then, afterward (they went back and changed)

steps.whatToRemember: In this version, the trust problem came from butchers remembering an older, easier opinion. Once that opinion was forgotten, they did the job the proper way and could be trusted.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the opposite order from the first version in step 26. There it went רבי מאיר then רבי יהודה. Here it goes רבי יהודה then רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: At first they held like Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: This is the easier method of removing the nerve, from step 26.

phrases.english: then they held like Rabbi Meir.

phrases.aramaic: כַּמָּה דַּהֲווֹ דְּכִירִי לַהּ לִדְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה – לָא מְהֵימְנֵי,
phrases.english: As long as they remembered Rabbi Yehuda's view, they were not believed,
but now that they have forgotten Rabbi Yehuda's view, they are believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִיקָּרָא סַבְרוּהָ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הֲדַר סַבְרוּהָ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The change is explained by a shift in הלכה and in what butchers remember, not by a change in their honesty.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רב נחמן meant butchers had become more honest.
steps.terutzMaskana: Butchers today only know רבי מאיר's method, so there is no worry they will take the old easy way, and they can be trusted.

steps.title: Who mentioned חלב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the חכמים in the משנה mention חלב, since the משנה was only talking about the גיד הנשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And about the חלב': who mentioned חלב at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to a wording problem in the משנה. The חכמים mention חלב even though nobody before them talked about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'and about the חלב' sound like a reply to someone who spoke about חלב. But the first opinion in the משנה only talked about the גיד הנשה, so the extra word seems to come from nowhere.

keyTerms.meaning: Who mentioned it? (it was never brought up)

phrases.english: 'And about the forbidden fat':
Forbidden fat, who mentioned it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל הַחֵלֶב – חֵלֶב, מַאן דְּכַר שְׁמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the question of trust and returns to the wording of the משנה quoted in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'and about the חלב' in the חכמים's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first opinion in the משנה never mentioned חלב, so the חכמים seem to be answering something nobody said.

steps.title: The משנה is short for a full argument about both
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means that רבי מאיר says butchers are not believed about the גיד הנשה or the חלב, and the חכמים say they are believed about both.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: they are not believed about it or about the חלב. And the חכמים say: they are believed about it and about the חלב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by filling in words the משנה left out. The first opinion also talked about חלב, so the חכמים were replying to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the משנה really covered both the גיד הנשה and the חלב, even though it only mentioned the nerve. Once we read it that way, the חכמים's 'and about the חלב' is a direct answer, and the problem goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means; the גמרא is filling in the full meaning

steps.whatToRemember: The argument in the משנה covers both the גיד הנשה and the חלב: the first opinion says butchers are not believed about either, and the חכמים say they are believed about both.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
They are not believed about it or about the forbidden fat,

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: נֶאֱמָנִין עָלָיו וְעַל הַחֵלֶב.
phrases.english: and the חכמים say: They are believed about it and about the forbidden fat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Fills in words the משנה left out.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the first opinion only spoke about the גיד הנשה, so the חכמים's mention of חלב made no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first opinion said butchers are not believed about the גיד הנשה or the חלב, and the חכמים argue on both.

steps.title: A Jew may send a non-Jew a thigh with the גיד הנשה inside
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows sending a thigh with the גיד הנשה still in it to a גוי, because the spot of the גיד is easy to recognize.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person may send a thigh to a non-Jew even though the גיד הנשה is still inside it, because its place can be recognized.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It says a Jew may give a non-Jew a thigh that still has the forbidden גיד הנשה in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might worry that the גוי will later sell the thigh to a Jew, who will eat the גיד by mistake. The משנה says there is no worry. Anyone can see where the גיד sits, so a Jew buying it would know to remove it.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A person may send a thigh to a non-Jew
that has the גיד הנשה inside it,
because its place is recognizable.
phrases.notes: The worry is that a Jew might later buy it back. Since the גיד's spot is obvious, that Jew would know to take it out.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹלֵחַ אָדָם יָרֵךְ לְגוֹי שֶׁגִּיד הַנָּשֶׁה בְּתוֹכָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion about trusting butchers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thigh with the גיד הנשה inside may be sent to a גוי, because the גיד's place is recognizable.

steps.title: A whole thigh is allowed, a cut thigh is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads into the משנה's reason: the permission only works for a whole thigh, not one that was cut up.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A whole thigh, yes. A cut thigh, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a lesson from the משנה's reason. If the thigh is whole you may send it, but if it is cut you may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allowed it only because the גיד's spot is easy to see. Once the thigh is cut into pieces, you can no longer tell where the גיד is. So the reason no longer works, and the permission falls away.

phrases.english: Gemara:
A whole thigh, yes, you may send it;
a cut thigh, no, you may not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a limit out of the משנה's reason in Step 33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The permission covers only a whole thigh, where the גיד's place can be seen. A cut thigh may not be sent.

steps.title: What situation is the משנה talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the משנה means, and starts testing a first option: a place where butchers do not announce.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If you say it is a place where they do not announce...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what exact situation the משנה has in mind, and begins to try one option. The sentence is not finished here. It sets up a challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether a Jew might buy meat from a גוי depends on local practice. The גמרא tests the case of a place where butchers do not announce, and it will soon show that this option causes a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
If you say (trying out an option)

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with?
If you say it is a place where they do not announce,
phrases.notes: He means Jewish butchers who don't announce when they sold a טריפה animal to a non-Jew. The thought finishes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין מַכְרִיזִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the limit in Step 34, the גמרא asks what setting the משנה describes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what kind of place is the משנה's rule about sending a thigh to a גוי said? The first option tested is a place where butchers do not announce.
